Pistons turn the large powered wheels of a steam locomotive, known collectively by this name.
A small swiveling wheel assembly ahead of a locomotive's drivers helps guide it into curves.

This onboard device releases grit ahead of powered wheels to improve grip on wet or icy rail.

Sensors at both ends of a section compare entering and leaving wheels in this alternative method of train detection.

Three-cylinder British locomotives could derive the middle cylinder's motion from the two outside sets using this linked arrangement.

Locomotive exhaust pulses draw air through the fire by passing up this tapered nozzle below the chimney.

Railway wheels are mounted slightly farther apart than the rails' inside faces; the lateral allowance between flange and rail is this.
In a three-part freight brake valve, the auxiliary reservoir, brake cylinder, and train pipe are governed by this later development of the original triple valve.

A rope or cable securing a vessel to a pier or fixed buoy has this name.

The angle between true north and magnetic north at a location is this correction applied to a compass course.

A route crossing every meridian at the same angle appears straight on a Mercator chart and has this name.

Contours and color bands show underwater relief on this specialized map.

Restricted water between a moving hull and a nearby bank accelerates, pulling the stern toward the bank in this effect.
Vapor bubbles forming and collapsing on propeller blades cause noise, erosion, and lost thrust in this process.

A hull's underwater volume divided by the rectangular block defined by its length, breadth, and draught yields this coefficient.
